title: Vector Similarity Search (DiskANN)
overview:
In this project you will add **vector similarity search** to EduDBMS, enabling queries like:

```sql
CREATE TABLE photos (id INTEGER, path VARCHAR, embedding VECTOR(512));
INSERT INTO photos VALUES (1, '/img/dog.jpg', [0.12, 0.45, ...]);
SELECT * FROM photos ORDER BY embedding <-> [0.33, 0.21, ...] LIMIT 5;
```

This is inspired by [pgvector](https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector), which extends PostgreSQL with vector operations. Vector similarity search powers **image retrieval** (find visually similar images), **semantic text search** (find documents matching a query meaning), and **multimodal search** (search images with text queries via CLIP embeddings).

Unlike previous projects that focused on a single DBMS layer, this project requires coordinated changes across **9 layers**. The diagram below shows how a vector query flows through each layer:

```
SQL: SELECT * FROM photos ORDER BY embedding <-> [0.3, 0.2] LIMIT 5
  │
  ▼
[Lexer]      embedding → IDENTIFIER
             <->       → OP_L2_DIST    ← new token
             [0.3,0.2] → LIT_VECTOR   ← new token
             LIMIT 5   → KW_LIMIT, 5
  │
  ▼
[Parser]     ORDER BY embedding <-> [0.3,0.2]
             → OrderByItem { DistanceExpr(ColumnRef, VectorLiteral) }
             LIMIT 5 → stmt.SetLimit(5)
  │
  ▼
[Planner]    Detects DistanceExpr in ORDER BY + LIMIT
             → LogicalVectorScan(photos, embedding, [0.3,0.2], 5)
             instead of LogicalSort + LogicalScan
  │
  ▼
[Optimizer]  LogicalVectorScan → PhysicalVectorScan
             (pass-through, no cost estimation needed)
  │
  ▼
[Executor]   VectorScanExec.Open():
               calls DiskANNIndex.Search([0.3,0.2], 5)
               → returns 5 nearest node_ids
             VectorScanExec.Next():
               returns table_rows[node_id] one at a time
  │
  ▼
[DiskANN]    Search: greedy beam search on proximity graph
             Build: Vamana algorithm (Search + RobustPrune per node)
             L2Distance: sqrt(sum((a[i]-b[i])^2))
```

Some layers are **already modified for you** (you study the changes). Other layers have **TODO functions you implement**. Each task below specifies exactly which files were changed, what code was added, and what you need to implement.

tasks.title: Layer 1-2: Type System & Vector Data Structures (Provided)
Layer 3-4: Lexer & AST Changes (Provided)
Layer 5: Parser — You Implement

functions.name: ParseDistanceExpr(unique_ptr<Expression> left) → unique_ptr<Expression>
functions.description:
Called when `ParseComparison()` sees `OP_L2_DIST` after parsing the left expression. The `left` parameter is already parsed (e.g., `ColumnRef("embedding")`). You need to:
1. Consume the `<->` token
2. Parse the right expression (the vector literal)
3. Return a `DistanceExpr` wrapping both

Example input: `embedding <-> [1.0, 2.0]`
- `left` = `ColumnRef("embedding")` (already parsed)
- You consume `<->` and parse `[1.0, 2.0]` → `VectorLiteral`
- Return `DistanceExpr(left, right)`
hints: `auto right = ParsePrimary()` parses the vector literal.

functions.name: ParseLimit(SelectStatement& stmt)
functions.description:
Called after `ParseOrderBy()`. If the next token is `KW_LIMIT`, consume it and parse the integer value.

Example: `... ORDER BY x LIMIT 5;`
- Token stream at this point: `KW_LIMIT`, `LIT_INTEGER("5")`, `SEMICOLON`
- You consume LIMIT, read 5, call `stmt.SetLimit(5)`

If there is no LIMIT keyword, do nothing and return.

tasks.title: Layer 6: Planner — You Implement

functions.name: TryPlanVectorScan(const SelectStatement& stmt) → unique_ptr<LogicalPlanNode>
functions.description:
Detect if this query is a vector similarity search. The pattern is:
- `ORDER BY` contains exactly one `DistanceExpr`
- `LIMIT` is set
- Single table (no joins)

If the pattern matches, return a `LogicalVectorScan`. Otherwise return `nullptr` (the normal planner will handle it).

Example: `SELECT * FROM photos ORDER BY embedding <-> [0.3, 0.2] LIMIT 5`
- `stmt.GetOrderBy()[0].expr` is a `DistanceExpr`
- `DistanceExpr::GetColumn()` → `ColumnRef("embedding")`
- `DistanceExpr::GetTarget()` → `VectorLiteral("[0.3, 0.2]")`
- `stmt.GetLimit()` → 5
- `stmt.GetFromTables()[0]` → `"photos"`
- Return `LogicalVectorScan("photos", "embedding", target, 5)`
hints: If `dist` is null → not a vector query → return nullptr.

tasks.title: Layer 7: Optimizer (Provided)
Layer 8: DiskANN Index — You Implement

functions.name: L2Distance(const Vector& a, const Vector& b) → float
functions.description: Euclidean distance: `sqrt(sum((a[i] - b[i])^2))`. Used by Search, Build, and RobustPrune.

functions.name: Search(const Vector& query, uint32_t k) → vector<pair<uint32_t, float>>
hints: Only explore if distance < farthest result (pruning).
Trim result to `beam_width_` after each insertion.

functions.name: RobustPrune(uint32_t node_id, vector<pair<uint32_t, float>>& candidates)
functions.description:
Select up to `max_degree_` diverse neighbors.

```
sort candidates by distance
selected = []
for each candidate c (closest first):
    if |selected| >= max_degree_: break
    if L2Distance(any_selected, c) < dist(node, c):
        skip (c is "covered" by existing neighbor)
    else:
        selected.add(c)
adjacency_[node_id] = selected
```

The diversity check prevents all neighbors from clustering in one direction.
hints: Inner loop: for each already-selected neighbor, compute `L2Distance(selected, candidate)`.
If any selected neighbor is closer to the candidate than the node is → skip.

functions.name: Build(const vector<Vector>& vectors)
functions.description:
Vamana graph construction:

```
1. Store vectors, allocate adjacency lists
2. entry_point_ = 0
3. For each node: assign R random neighbors (initial graph)
4. Shuffle node order
5. For each node i (in shuffled order):
    a. candidates = Search(vectors[i], beam_width)
    b. Remove self from candidates
    c. RobustPrune(i, candidates)  → sets adjacency_[i]
    d. For each j in adjacency_[i]:
         Add reverse edge: j → i
         If |adjacency_[j]| > max_degree_:
             Re-prune j
```
hints: Use `std::mt19937 rng(42)` for deterministic random init.
Random init: for each node, pick `max_degree_` random other nodes.
Reverse edge: `if i not in adjacency_[j], add it`.
Re-prune: compute distances for j's neighbors, call `RobustPrune(j, ...)`.

tasks.title: Layer 9: Executor — You Implement

functions.name: VectorScanExec::Open()
functions.description:
Call the DiskANN index to find the K nearest neighbors of `query_vector_`.

1. `auto results = index_->Search(query_vector_, limit_);`
2. Extract `node_id` from each result into `result_ids_`.
3. Reset `idx_ = 0`.

functions.name: VectorScanExec::Next() → optional<Row>
functions.description:
Return the next row from the table in similarity order.

1. If `idx_ >= result_ids_.size()`, return `nullopt`.
2. Get `node_id = result_ids_[idx_++]`.
3. Return `(*table_rows_)[node_id]`.
hints: Table rows are indexed by the same node_id used by the DiskANN index.

testing.note: This project is independent of Project #1-#6. Recall tests compare against brute-force KNN — your DiskANN must achieve at least the stated recall thresholds.
testing.platforms: macOS or Linux, on either Intel or ARM. On Windows, build inside WSL: a native Windows toolchain is refused, because the reference libraries these downloads carry are built for macOS and Linux only.

hints: Read Tasks 1-2 and 5 first (provided code). You need to understand the data flow before implementing.
Start with L2Distance (8 lines) — everything depends on it.
Then ParseDistanceExpr + ParseLimit (13 lines total) — run proj7_test to verify SQL parsing works.
Then Search — you can test it on a graph with random neighbors before Build is ready.
Then RobustPrune, then Build — these make the graph quality high enough to pass recall tests.
TryPlanVectorScan is pattern-matching: does ORDER BY have a DistanceExpr? Is there a LIMIT?
VectorScanExec is the easiest (10 lines total) — implement it last.
The DiskANN paper (Subramanya et al., NeurIPS 2019) has the full algorithm. Our implementation simplifies it (single pass, in-memory, no PQ compression).

submission.where: Upload the archive to PLMS (https://plms.postech.ac.kr) under Project #7 before the deadline. Submissions sent by email, or left anywhere else, are not collected.
submission.note: Keep the original directory layout inside the archive (src/…), so the files drop straight back into the project tree. Submit only the files you edited: no build/ directory, no compiled objects, no reference libraries.

blocks.text: **For each module below, write one expression that is always true of it** — true before any of its functions is called, and true again every time one of them returns. It may go false in the middle of a function; that is what makes it worth writing down.
The expression is symbols, not words:
If something is hard to put in symbols, define it as a variable in words, then use the variable in the expression:

code: P = the spaces with a car in them
F = the spaces that are empty
for i in 0 .. total_spaces-1:  i in P or i in F

blocks.text: A module holds several such expressions true at once. Pick one and get it right; you do not have to find them all.
**For each function you wrote, show your expression is still true when it returns.** A line or two each, grouped by module.
If a function cannot affect the expression, say so in one line. If it could, say which step keeps it true.
